# Elite Bot Studios

> Embedded Intelligence. Real-World Power.

Elite Bot Studios is an independent engineering initiative and evolving portfolio by Muhammad Shahzaib Abbas, an Electrical Engineering undergraduate at the National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), Pakistan. His academic direction is power engineering; related interests include embedded systems, power electronics, electronics, control, and intelligent energy systems.

The public portfolio separates concepts and educational models from project evidence. The Smart Energy Monitoring entry is a concept, not a prototype. Calculator plots are generated from documented ideal models; no hardware measurements are implied.

## Pages

- [Home](https://elitebotstudios.me/): interactive conceptual power-control system, engineering focus, project direction, and academic profile.
- [Projects](https://elitebotstudios.me/projects.html): evidence-labelled records, a conceptual system architecture, and separately marked future directions.
- [DC Energy Monitor](https://elitebotstudios.me/projects/dc-energy-monitor.html): a running software model of a low-voltage DC energy-monitoring system — configurable source and five load models, a sensing chain with gain, offset, noise and ADC quantisation, sampled power and trapezoidal energy accumulation. Includes five guided experiments, CSV export and an architecture explanation. Attributed as AI-assisted work; no hardware exists.
- [Smart Energy Monitoring project record](https://elitebotstudios.me/projects/smart-energy-monitoring.html): the case study for Project 01 — problem, objective, system design, mathematics, verification results, trade-offs, limitations and the hardware plan. Software Model V1 is verified; the hardware prototype is explicitly not built.
- [Power-stage sizing utility](https://elitebotstudios.me/projects/power-stage-utility.html): a published software demonstration. Sizes an ideal buck inductor at the worst-case input voltage (V_in,max, where ripple is largest), reports current stress, the CCM boundary and an output-capacitance estimate with optional ESR, derating and transient terms. Formulas, a worked calculation and two test suites (a reference-case suite and an independent switching-cycle simulation) are published with the source. Attributed as AI-assisted work rather than the founder's independent engineering.
- [Expertise](https://elitebotstudios.me/expertise.html): academic foundation, practical exploration, and research interests linked as a system map.
- [Engineering Lab](https://elitebotstudios.me/lab.html): five Markdown-authored technical notes, including [PWM fundamentals](https://elitebotstudios.me/lab/pwm-duty-frequency-resolution.html), [the ideal buck-converter CCM model](https://elitebotstudios.me/lab/buck-converter-ccm-model.html), [ADC resolution and quantization](https://elitebotstudios.me/lab/adc-resolution-quantization.html), simulation versus measurement, and documentation.
- [Engineering tools](https://elitebotstudios.me/tools.html): seven browser-side models: an interactive ideal-CCM buck converter explorer, a PWM signal laboratory (duty, frequency, timing, average and RMS), and five component/sizing calculators.
- [Capabilities & collaboration](https://elitebotstudios.me/services.html): transparent areas of study and possible collaboration.
- [About](https://elitebotstudios.me/about.html): founder profile and academic/research direction.
- [Contact](https://elitebotstudios.me/contact.html): posts to the site's own /api/contact endpoint. If mail delivery is not configured on a deployment, the endpoint reports that and the page opens a local email draft instead, telling the visitor that nothing was transmitted.

## Project 01 artefacts

- Model: `energy-monitor/model/dcem.js` (dependency-free, UMD; the same file the instrument runs and the tests import).
- Reference tests: `energy-monitor/tests/dcem-reference.test.js` (cases A–G, 67 assertions).
- Independent tests: `energy-monitor/tests/dcem-independent.test.js` (10 groups, 594 checks).
- Page contract test: `energy-monitor/tests/energy-monitor-page.test.js`.
- Reference datasets: `energy-monitor/examples/*.csv` with metadata headers.
- Documentation: `energy-monitor/docs/` — model, requirements, architecture, limitations, hardware plan, reproduction.

## Sources and limits

- The buck explorer uses the ideal steady-state CCM duty and inductor-ripple relationships at the single input voltage entered. Over an input range, ripple and the CCM boundary are worst at the highest input voltage; the power-stage sizing utility handles that range explicitly. Neither model solves DCM, device losses, controller dynamics, thermal behavior, or switching transitions.
- Other calculators also show their assumptions and intended limits on their pages.
- The calculator UI processes inputs in the browser and does not send them to a calculation API.
- The DC Energy Monitor is a simulation. It models an ideal sensing chain; it is not a measurement of any hardware, and no accuracy claim about physical devices follows from it. Its hardware prototype has not been built.
